builds.howItPlays: Lightning Rush looks at your top three cards, keeps one and puts the rest in your trash, and each card you play from the trash charges Kennen so he can give an attacker +2 Might, which lets cheap units like Traveling Merchant win early fights. Rhasa the Sunderer costs 10 but gets 1 cheaper for every card in your trash, and The Harrowing plays a Baron Nashor from your trash without paying its Energy cost.
builds.whyYou: You like a deck that uses its discard pile as a second hand. Every early turn has a double purpose: attack with a cheap unit, and put the right cards in the trash for later. You enjoy the sums, like how many cards Rhasa needs in the trash before you can afford it this turn, or whether to spend Kennen's charge now or hold it for a better attack. You don't mind that the big payoff takes a few turns to set up, because your small units are scoring points while you wait. If a 10-cost unit arriving on turn four sounds more fun than playing one on turn ten, this Kennen suits you.

builds.howItPlays: You answer their units with Cull the Weak, which makes each player kill one of their own units, and save The Ruination, a 9-cost spell that kills every unit, for when the board gets away from you. Meanwhile Pack of Wonders returns Treasure Trove to your hand each turn, and each time Trove leaves the board you draw a card and gain a rune, until a big unit like Rhasa the Sunderer can land and take over.
builds.whyYou: You'd rather answer everything your opponent plays than race them. You like having almost no early units and a hand full of removal, and you like the small loop of bouncing Treasure Trove with Pack of Wonders each turn for another card and another rune. Games run long and you're fine with that, because each turn you have more cards and runes than they do. Some games they will score points before your answers line up, and you can live with that. If wiping the board and then landing one huge unit sounds better than swarming with small ones, this Kennen suits you.
builds.ratingNotes:
New 2026-09-25 (from the deck picks, style Ruination Control Kennen, the lead agent's merge of grey-zone styles 3 and 4 at 0.57). Both styles loop Pack of Wonders with Treasure Trove, answer with Cull the Weak and The Ruination, and ramp with Seal of Unity. Only the Champion differs: Storm of Shuriken or Keeper of Balance. The style name comes from the picks, and the label is the tool's and both raters'. tools.ts style: Control 2.5/4/7/5, mean of 2.
Scored decks:
- Kennen, Storm of Shuriken (Ruben Smith; 10 likes, 3127 views, 2026-06-25, legal) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/715fb684-5979-4ac0-8be1-62b9305f3ba0 Control 2.5/3.5/7/4.5
- Control Post SD (Blybe; 1 like, pre-ban, legal) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/c6c9d1b9-962b-407b-b7c7-a7d63db9c3e1 Control 2.5/4/7/5. The rater judged Control where the scorer suggested Midrange, because Stance landed at 4. The list has almost no early units and plays 8 removal cards plus 2 Ruination.
Adjustments, the same on both: Pace -1, because Forgotten Monument blocks scoring there until turn three and The Papertree ramps both players, and both lengthen the game. Complexity +0.5, because the Legend empowers from Flow spells and its Assault 2 must be timed. No Axis had a formula-judgment gap of 2 or more. On Ruben's list, Stance was scorer 4 vs judged 2.5 and Complexity was 6 vs 7.5.
Cards that decided each Axis:
- Pace: 0 or 1 cheap units against 6 or 7 cards costing 5+ (The Ruination, Rhasa the Sunderer, Vanguard Armory, Baron Nashor, Rift Herald, Angler Beast).
- Stance: 10 to 17 answers (Cull the Weak, Wind and Ghosts, Lacerate, Gust, Star-Crossed, The List, The Ruination) against 4 to 7 pressure cards.
- Complexity: the Pack of Wonders and Treasure Trove loop, Flow spells (Lightning Rush, Lacerate, Up from the Deep) and Fizz replaying spells from the trash.
- Variance: no luck cards. Ramp and engine pieces push the formula up. Removal and card flow pull it down, and so does The Ruination, the only swing card, on Blybe's list.
Legend ability: when you play a card from anywhere other than your hand, Kennen is empowered. [Action] Disempower him and exhaust him to give a unit Assault 2 this turn.
Also played: none.
Confidence: medium. By the letter the bar is high (7 decks, 2 strong), but it rests on the merge, and only two legal lists exist. Neither is within 0.35 of the medoid, so the display is the strongest legal list.
For the reviewer: the display list predates the latest ban but contains no banned card. Krashy's 19-like Control Kennen (video) vouches for the style but is illegal because of Stacked Deck. The copy names Rhasa the Sunderer, which only Ruben's list plays. Blybe's list closes with Baron Nashor and Rift Herald instead.
